definition: AI Dungeon is a single-player/multiplayer text adventure game which uses artificial intelligence (AI) to generate content and allows players to create and share adventures and custom prompts.
details: The game's first version was made available in May 2019, and its second version (initially called AI Dungeon 2) was released on Google Colaboratory in December 2019. It was later ported that same month to its current cross-platform web application. The AI model was then reformed in July 2020.

explainer.lead: AI Dungeon is a text adventure game whose story is generated by artificial intelligence in response to whatever a player chooses to do or say. Instead of selecting from a fixed script, players can explore pre-made settings or create and publish their own adventures, alone or with others.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a storytelling friend who makes up the next part of an adventure whenever you say what your character does. You might choose a fantasy world, decide to open a mysterious door, and then read what happens next. You can also create adventures for other people or take turns telling a story with friends.
tiers.practitioner: Players interact through Do, Say, Story, and See commands, with Do, Say, and Story shaping the narrative and See generating an image without affecting gameplay. Memory instructions, blank prompts, and undo, redo, and editing controls help manage continuity and correct weak output; multiplayer hosts can also supervise and modify the AI's responses.
tiers.paperLevel: AI Dungeon can be described as interactive conditional generation: next_content = AI_model(setting, prior_story_context, player_input). The original version used an early GPT-2 model, AI Dungeon 2 used the 1.5-billion-parameter GPT-2, and the Dragon and Griffin models introduced in July 2020 used versions of GPT-3. Players may need to revise recent events or supply remembered elements to improve the generated narrative.

explainer.example: A player starts a fantasy adventure and enters “Do: Open the locked door in the abandoned tower.” The AI generates what happens next; the player can then use Say to question a character or Story to establish an event that should shape the continuing adventure.

usedIn.name: Single-player interactive fiction
usedIn.detail: Players choose a setting and character options, then develop an AI-generated storyline through free-form text input.

usedIn.name: Online and local multiplayer storytelling
usedIn.detail: Several players control separate characters and take turns in one session, either across devices or on a shared device.

usedIn.name: Community-created adventures
usedIn.detail: Players can describe custom settings, publish the resulting adventures, browse others' work, and leave comments.

explainer.intuition: AI Dungeon works like an improvisational dungeon master: the player supplies actions, dialogue, or story events, and the AI writes a response. Its freedom comes from generating content during play rather than requiring every possible storyline to be written in advance.
howItWorks: Choose a configured setting such as fantasy, mystery, apocalyptic, cyberpunk, or zombies, or describe a custom adventure.
Select setting-specific options, such as a character class in a fantasy adventure.
Enter an action with Do, dialogue with Say, or narrative information with Story; See instead produces an image.
The AI uses the adventure's context and the input to generate the next part of the story.
Continue, submit a blank input for more content, or use memory and editing controls to guide or revise later events.
explainer.whyItMatters: It was one of the only known commercial applications based on GPT-2 and demonstrated how a language model could support open-ended, player-directed entertainment. Its development from a hackathon project to a cross-platform game also connected AI-generated text with multiplayer play and user-published content.
misconceptions: The original version did not accept any action a player wanted; it offered a finite list of possible actions.
See does not advance or alter gameplay—it generates an image from a description.
Multiplayer uses third-person narration, unlike the second-person narration of single-player stories.
